title: Rukmini's letter
hookLine: a princess is about to be married to the wrong man, so she writes a letter and finds someone to carry it
tomorrow: who stole the jewel that shone like the sun?

lines: A LETTER ON THE ROAD TO DWARAKA.
cards: A letter is traveling by road from the kingdom of Vidarbha to the city of Dwaraka. The man carrying it is an old brahmin, trusted, sworn to deliver it into one pair of hands.

The woman who wrote it is the king's daughter, Rukmini. Her brother has arranged her marriage to a king she doesn't want: Shishupala, the man we met earlier this year at Yudhishthira's great rite. The wedding is coming.
Her family has decided. And Rukmini has decided too, quietly, on her own.

teach.h: I HAVE HEARD, AND I HAVE CHOSEN.
teach.b: In Dwaraka, Krishna receives the brahmin, washes his feet, feeds him, and only then asks why he's come. The brahmin hands him the letter, and the Bhagavata lets us read it, in paraphrase.
I have heard of your qualities, Rukmini writes, and hearing them, my mind has gone to you and won't come back. I've set shame aside. I have chosen you.
Come and take my hand. Don't let the king of Chedi take what is yours, like a jackal stealing a lion's share. Then she gives him a plan.

Come to Vidarbha before the wedding, unseen, with your forces. She knows her family's customs: before the wedding, the bride walks out of the city to the temple of the goddess Ambika. That's where you'll find me.
And if you don't come, she writes, she will give up her life, and keep hoping for him life after life. Rukmini has never seen Krishna. She has only heard about him.
That's a teaching, not a detail: Prahlada's list of the nine ways of devotion begins with shravana, hearing, and it's why Hindus still gather for days just to listen to the Bhagavata read aloud.
But she doesn't stop at hearing. She writes, she plans, she risks. Krishna answers right away, setting out in his chariot that same night.
On the appointed day, Rukmini prays at the goddess's temple, walks out, and he's there.

teach.h: SHRAVANA: SHE NEVER SAW HIM. SHE HEARD.
teach.b: He lifts her into his chariot in front of everyone.
There's a fight; her brother chases them, and loses.
In Dwaraka, they marry. Some devotees hear Rukmini as the soul that has heard of God, chosen God, and taken the first step.

how: Rukmini is worshipped beside Krishna in temples, and some Hindus recite her letter from the Bhagavata, especially when praying for a good marriage; at a Bhagavata saptaha, seven days of the book read aloud, simply listening is the devotion.

o: the goddess whose temple stood outside the city
the queen who raised Krishna in the cowherd village
the princess who heard of Krishna, chose him and wrote

p: the temple of the goddess Ambika

s: Rukmini had met Krishna many times before she wrote
she had only heard of his qualities. hearing was where her devotion began.
Rukmini's letter includes a practical plan
come before the wedding, unseen, and find me at the goddess's temple outside the city.
Krishna waits a long time before answering
he sets out in his chariot that same night.

games.q: you're Rukmini. your family has promised you to a man you don't want. the wedding is coming. what do you do?
o: write to Krishna, choose him, and give him a plan.
games.why: she writes the letter, sends it with a brahmin, and tells Krishna exactly where to find her: at the goddess's temple.

practice: Rukmini's devotion started with hearing, so for this sit, simply listen: the far sounds, the near ones, the sound of your own breath, received one by one without naming or judging them.
If you pray, let a name you love be the sound you return to; if you don't, return to the breath whenever the mind wanders.

wordCard.voice: Rukmini, the princess of Vidarbha who became Krishna's queen. Today, her letter: devotion that begins with shravana, hearing, and then writes, plans and acts.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: Rukmini, the princess of Vidarbha, Krishna's queen, worshipped beside him.

carryVoice: Your line: shravana, devotion begins by hearing. Rukmini heard, then chose. Day nine hundred eighty-four, done.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.52 (Rukmini's letter carried to Dwaraka)
